title: Thoroughbred Kidnapping Case
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0933.txt, subs_resolved/0934.txt (689 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi, Officer Chiba) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities actually involved. case_type: insurance_fraud staged as a kidnapping (no human victim; the racehorse White Spirits is the ostensible target). Corrections vs. the old low-fidelity file: the old file correctly named Kozo Tokuyoshi as mastermind and kept `case_type: fraud`, but it flattened the whole plot into two generic events and treated the other four staff as undifferentiated 'suspects' equally complicit with him. The transcript actually shows the opposite power relationship: Tokuyoshi coerced trainer Hase, stable hand Nagaura and jockey Kakuta (using debts he held over them) to kill White Spirits and stage a kidnapping so he could collect the horse's life-insurance payout after his reckless foreign investments went bad; the three secretly refused to kill the horse, hid him alive at their old stable (Kitado Stables) with a look-alike brother (White Legion) substituted in his place, disguised themselves and separately hired Kogoro Mori hoping a famous detective's presence would scare Tokuyoshi into calling off the scheme, then falsely reported to Tokuyoshi that the horse was dead once he went ahead anyway. Trailer driver Shiomi was their accomplice; his claimed wife-and-child kidnapping (used to justify diverting the trailer) is explicitly cast in doubt by Kogoro's closing remarks as possibly staged, not a real hostage-taking. The old file also omitted that the '100 million yen' ransom Tokuyoshi appeared to pay was never real money -- Kogoro proves the bag was stuffed with torn magazines from Tokuyoshi's own house, i.e. Tokuyoshi self-staged the entire ransom drop as a prop for his insurance claim and 'victim' narrative. None of this nuance (decoy horse, self-staged ransom, protective rather than complicit staff, doubted secondary kidnapping claim) existed in the old file; it is added here from the full transcript.

clues.desc: The insurance payout was requested one day before the bloody horse blanket was even discovered, showing Tokuyoshi knew of the horse's supposed death before it was public knowledge.
Of the two trailer tire-track sets at the side road, one was much shallower, as if nothing was inside it -- inconsistent with a real horse having been swapped there.
The convenience-store footage showing a trailer leaving the side road is timestamped three days before the transport day, proving that scene was staged evidence, not a live swap.
A torn magazine cover left on a rack in Tokuyoshi's living room matches a torn magazine stuffed inside the supposed 100-million-yen ransom bag.
Horse hair recovered at Kitado Stables includes both White Spirits' fur and White Legion's, proving the two horses were swapped there, not during transport.
